metadata.title: Will Kacmarek - Clear to suit up Sunday
metadata.description: Kacmarek (hamstring) doesn't have a designation for Sunday battle against the Patriots, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.
metadata.analysis: Kacmarek dealt with a hamstring injury this week and logged limited practices Wednesday and Thursday. However, he was able to upgrade to a full session Friday and has thus been cleared to play Sunday. Kacmarek should serve in his usual role as the No. 2 tight end who focuses primarily on blocking.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek - Remains limited at practice Thursday
metadata.description: Kacmarek (hamstring) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
metadata.analysis: Kacmarek has now been limited two straight days to begin Week 8 prep while tending to a hamstring injury. He'll almost certainly enter the weekend with a designation for Sunday's contest against the Patriots if he isn't able to practice in full Friday. Kacmarek has worked primarily as a blocker this season, but he does have three catches for 24 yards on six targets through six games.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek - Nursing hamstring injury
metadata.description: Kacmarek (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Kacmarek may have picked up the injury during the Dolphins' Week 7 win over the Jets, when he logged 34 snaps (29 on offense, five on special teams) without showing up on the box score otherwise. The rookie third-rounder will have two more opportunities to return to practice in at least a limited capacity before Sunday's game against the Patriots.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek - Blocks in win
metadata.description: Kacmarek played 29 offensive snaps and five special-teams snaps but did not appear in the box score of the Dolphins' 28-25 win over the Jets on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Kacmarek played 45 percent of the Dolphins' offensive snaps. The No. 2 tight end's blocking role was starkly contrasted by Greg Dulcich's team-leading target share.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek - Limited again but expects to play
metadata.description: Kacmarek (hamstring) was limited in Thursday's practice, but he said he expects to play Sunday versus the Jets, Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post reports.
metadata.analysis: Kacmarek is dealing with a hamstring issue, though it's not clear when he suffered the injury given that Miami was on bye this past weekend. Regardless, the rookie tight end is anticipating being on the field Week 7 despite being limited in practice both Wednesday and Thursday. Kacmarek hasn't been a major factor in Miami's passing game thus far, recording just three catches on six targets for 24 yards through five contests.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek (hamstring) limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Will Kacmarek (hamstring) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Kacmarek picked up a hamstring injury at some point and was limited at practice on Wednesday as a result. His potential absence this week wouldn't have much of an impact for fantasy purposes, however.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek - Limited practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Kacmarek (hamstring) was a limited participant at the Dolphins' practice Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
metadata.analysis: Kacmarek is dealing with an apparent hamstring injury coming out of Miami's bye week in Week 6. The tight end will have two more chances to log a full practice prior to Sunday's matchup with the Jets.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek Worth a Deep-League Look
metadata.description: Miami Dolphins tight end Will Kacmarek played more snaps last week against the Vikings than veteran tight end Greg Dulcich. Kacmarek got two targets and caught one for 15 yards, which was actually the second-highest total of receiving yards on the team in Miami's 15-10 loss to the Vikings. QB Malik Willis threw for just 85 yards in the loss, and the passing offense has been anemic all season. The third-round rookie out of Ohio State could continue to grow as an option, though, and has also been effective as a blocker in the team's run-heavy scheme. Against the Bengals this week, Kacmarek is only the No. 57 TE in RotoBaller's Week 5 rankings, but it is worth watching if he can seize the starting job and find enough opportunities to make an impact in a Miami offense searching for playmakers. He's a Dynasty stash worth considering in extremely deep leagues, but for now, he's just a rookie option to watch in standard-sized leagues.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek - Goes catchless in debut
metadata.description: Kacmarek failed to haul in his only target during Miami's loss to the Raiders on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Kacmarek was in the team's starting lineup for his regular-season debut but ended up seeing limited action, playing just 14 of the 56 offensive snaps in addition to six snaps on special teams. While the 23-year-old primarily functions as a blocker, he will still look to see an increased role during next week's matchup against the 49ers.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek sees one target in Week 1
metadata.description: Will Kacmarek failed to catch his only target in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Kacmarek saw minimal involvement as part of an underwhelming Miami offense in the season opener, finishing last in the team in targets. The tight end can remain off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 2 contest against the San Francisco 49ers.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek - Good to go for Sunday
metadata.description: Kacmarek (calf) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Las Vegas, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
metadata.analysis: The rookie third-round pick upgraded to full practice participation Friday after being limited earlier in the week. Greg Dulcich is Miami's top receiving threat at tight end, but Kacmarek could play a lot of snaps as a blocker and see a few targets here and there.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek (calf) off injury report Sunday
metadata.description: Will Kacmarek is off the injury report for Sunday's game against Raiders.
metadata.analysis: Kacmarek is good to go as had been reported.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek (calf) expected to play Sunday
metadata.description: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said he expects to have TE Will Kacmarek available for the opener on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Kacmarek has been limited in practice all week. He is on track to be good to go for Sunday's game against the Raiders.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek - Limited again
metadata.description: Kacmarek (calf) was a limited participant in practice for the second day in a row Thursday, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.
metadata.analysis: The tight end emerged from the Dolphins' last preseason game with an undisclosed issue that was eventually revealed to be a calf injury. He appears to still be dealing with it, though he did tell Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald on Wednesday that he expects to play in Miami's season opener Sunday against Las Vegas. The third-round pick is the backup to Greg Dulcich on the depth chart.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek - Limited at practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Kacmarek (calf) was limited during Wednesday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
metadata.analysis: Kacmarek practiced in full Monday, though his limited participation Wednesday is not an encouraging sign heading into the Week 1 meeting with Las Vegas. The 2026 No. 87 overall pick appeared in 14 games for Ohio State in 2025, totaling 15 catches for 168 yards and two touchdowns.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek practices Monday
metadata.description: Dolphins TE Will Kacmarek practiced on Monday.
metadata.analysis: Kacmarek previously missed time during camp.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek - Practices on Monday
metadata.description: Kacmarek (undisclosed) was a full participant in Monday's practice, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.
metadata.analysis: Kacmarek was considered week-to-week after the Dolphins' final preseason game against the Falcons on Aug. 28. The tight end has recovered from his undisclosed issue quickly and is back in action just in time for the team's Week 1 matchup with the Raiders.

metadata.title: Will Kacmarek - Won't practice this week
metadata.description: Kacmarek (undisclosed) is considered week-to-week as of Saturday, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.
metadata.analysis: Kacmarek did not play in Friday night's preseason finale against the Falcons. The rookie third-rounder played in the first two preseason games for the Dolphins, catching his sole target for three yards. The tight end is set to be the No. 2 option behind Greg Dulcich once the former regains his health.
